correctness.rationale: Scaling the (d−1)-dimensional slice of the power witness and integrating the resulting beta integral gives exponent (3−d)/2+(d−1)/2=1 and constants π/2, π, π²; in d=4 its pth power has an integrable boundary singularity exactly for p<2. For any signed L¹ input the spherical coarea density at t is |S^(d−2)|/|x| times (1−t²/|x|²)^((d−3)/2) for |x|>t. For t near 1 this bounds the angular absolute mean by O((1−t)^((d−3)/2)) times the L¹ mass of the terminal shell. That mass tends to zero; in d=4 for L² it is o((1−t)^(1/2)) by Hölder with the vanishing local L² norm, not just a global O bound. This gives o(1−t) in exactly the excluded cases, initially for a.e. t and then for the convex representatives at all interior t near 1 by Fatou and continuity along good t's. Recover the representatives by local averages. Convexity guarantees endpoint limits and Fatou on endpoint sequences makes them zero for a.e. direction already for any L¹ input when d≥3; reflection gives the left endpoint. Each profile is then nonpositive and its magnitude satisfies the stated chord bound. A nonzero profile must be strictly negative at 0, since an interior equality on its zero-endpoint chord forces affinity. The integrated coefficient is positive for nonzero f by Fourier-slice injectivity. It is in fact finite, since the chord bound can be integrated at a good t with finite angular mean (the finding's 'possibly infinite' is not needed). The inequality contradicts o(1−t), covering all excluded p by finite-measure inclusions. No finite symbolic checks are needed for these quantifiers.

value.rationale: The boundary distinguishes genuine examples from an empty convexity cone for the natural Euclidean ball, in the full signed nonradial setting. The excluded Hilbert endpoint in four dimensions and the L¹ obstruction in five and higher are substantive limits on which convex profiles are possible, beyond known examples or general smooth range descriptions.
